title: Kim Kardashian Taps Olympians Chloe Kim, Jutta Leerdam and More for New NikeSKIMS Campaign

body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Nike and Kim Kardashian are keeping the momentum going on one of the sportswear giant’s biggest celebrity partnerships.

	NikeSKIMS, the performance-wear brand created with Kardashian’s Skims, has unveiled its Fall 2026 “Edit 01” campaign, starring Olympians Jutta Leerdam, Chloe Kim, Anna Cockrell and Stephanie Au. The drop, available to shop Sept. 17 on both brands’ sites, arrives roughly a year after the joint venture made its retail debut.


	At the center of the 40-piece fall lineup is the new Performance Cotton Blend, a cotton-polyester fabric that incorporates Nike’s sweat-wicking Dri-FIT technology while maintaining “the feel of a worn-in T-shirt,” according to the brand. Tops in the fabric are garment-washed for a softer, slightly vintage finish. Elsewhere, NikeSKIMS is adding new shapes to its slick Satin Shine and more supportive Studio Stretch collections while bringing back established styles in seasonal colorways.

	The athlete-heavy casting has become something of a signature for the partnership. When NikeSKIMS made its retail debut last September, its Janicza Bravo-directed “Bodies at Work” campaign featured more than 50 athletes, including Serena Williams, Sha’Carri Richardson, Jordan Chiles, Nelly Korda and Kim — who returns for the new fall campaign after starring in the brand’s Spring 2026 gym push. Chloe Kim, notably, appeared in that inaugural NikeSKIMS rollout as well.

	Most recently, Kardashian stepped back in front of the camera in March for a second Spring 2026 push centered on gym essentials. The drop introduced Matte Shine Mix, alongside new colors and silhouettes across NikeSKIMS’ existing Shine, Airy and Matte categories, while Kardashian starred in imagery built around the proposition that workout clothes don’t have to choose between technical performance and a flattering fit.


	The latest campaign arrives as Kardashian’s relationship with Nike extends beyond NikeSKIMS itself. Earlier this summer, she made a cameo in Nike Football’s sprawling “Rip the Script” campaign alongside a cross-section of athletes and entertainers that included Cristiano Ronaldo, Kylian Mbappé, LeBron James, Travis Scott, Channing Tatum and fellow NikeSKIMS campaign star LISA.

	Shop NikeSKIMS’ newest collection here.

title: Sony TV Chief Keith Le Goy on Why PlayStation 5 FAST Channels Are Set Up for Success: 40-50 Million People ‘Incredibly Engaged With That Platform’
description: Sony struck synergy gold last month with the introduction of “Live TV on PS5,” an offering of more than 100 free ad-supported video channels availab
body:
Sony struck synergy gold last month with the introduction of “Live TV on PS5,” an offering of more than 100 free ad-supported video channels available via the PlayStation 5 video game console. 

	Backed by Sony Pictures Television, the venture is a chance to get the IP available to Sony TV (and the ads that can be tied to it) in front of a massive audience that is usually spending their time on gaming consoles, well, gaming.


	“The intent is that you have 40-50 million people on PlayStation 5 who are incredibly engaged with that platform, who are spending hours and hours and hours on their favorite games, but who also love to watch entertainment,”  chairman Keith Le Goy said Thursday during a panel conversation with Variety co-editor-in-chief Cynthia Littleton at the Variety Entertainment & Technology Summit presented by EY. “And therefore, if you can do two things, one is to curate the entertainment offering in a way that is pertinent to them, but also make it a very seamless transition from their gaming engagement to their entertainment engagement, then you have a real chance to engage an audience which traditionally has been a hard-to-reach audience for linear channels, a very hard-to-reach audience and a very attractive audience for advertisers.” 
	

	Goy added: “So if we can give that audience something that they’re going to like in an environment that they are comfortable with, give our channel partners an audience that they are going to be going after and give their advertisers an audience that’s valuable for them. That is one plus one equaling a lot more than two.”
	

	The PlayStation 5 FAST channel offering launched last month in the U.S. and Goy says the intention is to roll it out across “other countries in the coming months.” Goy sees the option as one unique to Sony, which distinguishes itself from many other players in Hollywood by having film, TV, music and gaming divisions all under one roof.

	“In many ways, people talk about the incursion of the tech companies into Hollywood, we were the first and I think we’ve learned a lot along the way,” You mentioned the relationship with PlayStation. “That’s the other thing that Sony has, that frankly a lot of other companies would love to have, is a gaming business and the level of engagement with gamers and gaming fans. That is what PlayStation has.”

	Goy says another area where Sony has “an unfair advantage, a particular right to win” is the anime industry through Crunchyroll and Aniplex.

	“Obviously, Crunchyroll has been an incredibly successful venture for us and has really allowed us to create this kind of anime ecosystem with Aniplex and Crunchyroll where we are able to super serve fans in a way that very few other companies, in fact, really no other company could do,” Goy says.

schema.headline: Sony TV Chief Keith Le Goy on Why PlayStation 5 FAST Channels Are Set Up for Success: 40-50 Million People ‘Incredibly Engaged With That Platform’

title: Dr. Orna Guralnik Gives Ciara Miller, Dylan Efron and Carl Schmidt a ‘Couples Therapy’ Session in New Samsung Galaxy Spot
description:

	Samsung i
body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission.

	Samsung is taking its latest Galaxy campaign to therapy.

	The tech giant has tapped “Couples Therapy” star Dr. Orna Guralnik to lead “Switchers,” a new campaign that centers a counseling session on the anxieties around ditching a longtime smartphone.

	The branded spots pair Guralnik with pairs of contrived couples such as “Summer House” star Ciara Miller and Dylan Efron, reality TV personalities Carl Schmidt and Aniya Harvey and former NFL players Nick Foles and Clay Matthews, who work through tech-centered issues such as  “brand loyalty,” “group-chat fears” and the “perceived hassle of transferring data between devices.”


	“My profession is all about change,” Guralnik, a clinical psychologist who stars in Showtime’s “Couples Therapy,” tells Variety. “People come to analysis when they’ve reached a certain point where they’re just repeating the same old patterns and having a hard time letting go or changing.”

	“The fact that Samsung decided to go toward this kind of psychological, even psychoanalytic language — even using language like, ‘What’s your defense?’ — it just tickled me a lot,” Guralnik continues. “What a great way to bring psychoanalytic and psychological language into mass culture, which is really what I’m doing with the show anyhow.”



	The commercial is the latest example of Samsung leaning on talent to market its Galaxy lineup. Earlier this year, the company added singer and rapper Audrey Nuna, model and influencer Haley Baylee and 11 other creators across music, gaming, fashion and culture to its #TeamGalaxy roster around the Galaxy S26 launch. Samsung also  enlisting K-pop talent including Eric Nam for its Galaxy Experience in February. 


	Samsung’s latest Galaxy Z lineup now spans three foldable models: the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, Z Fold8 and Z Flip8. The company says 30% of Galaxy Z Flip8 buyers since launch have switched from a competing smartphone brand, while the Fold8 and Fold8 Ultra are also bringing in a higher proportion of competitive switchers than the previous Fold7 generation.

	That makes convincing longtime iPhone and other smartphone users to defect a central part of Samsung’s sales pitch. The campaign highlights Smart Switch, which transfers contacts, photos, videos, messages, apps and settings from iOS or Android devices, alongside cross-platform RCS messaging and Samsung’s broader suite of Galaxy AI features.

	Guralnik even tested that proposition closer to home with her teenage son, whom she describes as highly resistant to changing phones. “He was constantly worried about how easy it would be to switch,” she says. “Would he lose all his contacts? Would he lose all his chains of messages with his friends? His photos? All of that.”

	Once he made the jump, she says, his concerns largely mirrored the barriers Samsung had built the campaign around.

	“They really dug deep into people’s anxieties and addressed them,” Guralnik says. “So, touché to Samsung.”

schema.headline: Dr. Orna Guralnik Gives Ciara Miller, Dylan Efron and Carl Schmidt a ‘Couples Therapy’ Session in New Samsung Galaxy Spot

title: Greta Gerwig Says ‘Narnia’ Is Inspired by David Bowie, Confirms Meryl Streep Is Voicing Aslan: ‘I Wanted Someone Profound but Not Pretentious’
description: Greta Gerwig is reuniting with her “Little Women” star Meryl Streep on “Narnia,” the director’s adaptation of the C.S. Lewis fantasy series. Streep
body:
Greta Gerwig is reuniting with her “Little Women” star Meryl Streep on “Narnia,” the director’s adaptation of the C.S. Lewis fantasy series. Streep is voicing Aslan, the mythical lion who creates the mystical world of Narnia.

	“I wanted someone who was profound but not pretentious, who had gravitas but not morose self-seriousness. Someone who could communicate depth and pathos as well as joy and delight,” Gerwig told Empire in a cover story about the upcoming film. “I wanted someone who was older than 70, so there was a wisdom of experience, but who also had the capacity of fresh wonder, like a child. And also to be one of the greatest actors to ever do it. That list is not a long one.”
	

	David Bowie was a source of inspiration, both for the look of Aslan (who has multicolored eyes and a red-striped face in this version) as well as the essence of the movie, according to Gerwig. She described wanting the movie to be “big and transporting” and feel like a “rock opera.”


	“David Bowie saved my life. Paul McCartney saved my life. David Gilmour saved my life. Pete Townshend saved my life. Jimmy Page, Robert Plant,” Gerwig told Empire. “When I heard their music, I had this deep sense of [thinking], ‘You’re gonna be OK.’”

	As it relates to the fantasy adventure, she says, “Narnia is literally a world made out of music. It is a world sung to life by Aslan, and rock ’n’ roll to me felt like a world made out of music.”

	“The Magician’s Nephew” is Gerwig’s much-anticipated follow-up to “Barbie,” her Oscar-winning box office sensation starring Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling. “The Magician’s Nephew” serves as a prequel to “The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe” and follows two children, Digory and Polly, who are the first to discover the “Wood between the Worlds,” aka Narnia, after their uncle (Daniel Craig) gives them a magical ring. David McKenna, Beatrice Campbell, Emma Mackey, Carey Mulligan and Ciarán Hinds round out the cast.
	

	Previously slated for Thanksgiving 2026, “Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew” will open in theaters on Feb. 12, 2027, before landing on Netflix on April 2.

schema.headline: Greta Gerwig Says ‘Narnia’ Is Inspired by David Bowie, Confirms Meryl Streep Is Voicing Aslan: ‘I Wanted Someone Profound but Not Pretentious’

body:
Sep 17, 2026 11:19am PT	
	

			


			
			
	

									Getty Images
	

		
	
				
	Former President Barack Obama has picked his six guests for his “A Great Book” podcast to discuss the books that have had the biggest impact on his worldview — and on our society.

	“A Great Book With Barack Obama” is a six-episode series that debuts exclusively from Audible on Sept. 24, 2026. Later in the year, it will also be available on YouTube and everywhere you get your podcasts. The series is collaboration between Audible and Higher Ground, the production company founded by Barack and Michelle Obama.
	

	The guests in conversation with President Obama — and the books they’ll discuss — are:



Episode 1: Tom Hanks, Academy, Emmy, and Golden Globe Award-winning actor, on “Gilead” by Marilynne Robinson
Episode 2: Ta-Nehisi Coates, National Book Award-winning author, MacArthur Fellow, and journalist, on “The Fire Next Time” by James Baldwin
Episode 3: Jill Lepore, Pulitzer Prize-winning historian and journalist, on “All the King’s Men” by Robert Penn Warren
Episode 4: Ben Rhodes, former National Security Advisor and author, on “Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy” by John le Carré
Episode 5: Percival Everett, Pulitzer Prize and National Book Award-winning author, on “Song of Solomon” by Toni Morrison
Episode 6: Lauren Groff, three-time National Book Award finalist and New York Times bestselling author, on “All the Pretty Horses” by Cormac McCarthy



	The podcast is described like this by Audible and Higher Ground: “Reflecting on identity, power, memory and culture, the conversations between President Obama and his guests explore one central question: What do the stories we love tell us about the world we live in and the world we want to create?”

	Previous Audible and Higher Ground collaborations include “Michelle Obama: The Light Podcast” hosted by the First Lady; “Your Mama’s Kitchen: Conversations From the Heart of the Home” hosted by Michele Norris; “The Wonder of Stevie” hosted by Wesley Morris; Peabody Award-winner “Fela Kuti: Fear No Man,” hosted by Jad Abumrad; and “Reconstruction: The Unfinished Promise,” a collaboration with the History Channel and Pushkin Industries hosted by Malcolm Gladwell and featuring Barack Obama.
	


	
		More from Variety

schema.headline: Tom Hanks, Ta-Nehisi Coates and More Join Barack Obama’s ‘A Great Book’ Podcast at Audible

title: Barbra Streisand Condemns Trump’s ‘Unchecked Ego’ Over Kennedy Center Name Battle: ‘Galling and Painful to Witness’
description:
Barbra Streisand is speaking out against Pres. Donald Trump’s controversial handling of the Kennedy Center .

	“In 2008, I was deeply honored to be
body:
Barbra Streisand is speaking out against Pres. Donald Trump’s controversial handling of the Kennedy Center .

	“In 2008, I was deeply honored to be included in the 31st annual class of Kennedy Center Honorees,” Streisand wrote in a statement posted Thursday on her official website. “For me, and for so many artists, that honor represented something larger than a career recognition. It represented a belief in the importance of art to the life of a democracy.
	

	“That is why what is happening to the Kennedy Center is so galling and painful to witness,” she continued.


	Streisand’s remarks come on the heels of a district judge ordering the Kennedy Center on Thursday to provide at least 30 days’ notice in advance if a demolition or new construction is planned after Trump threatened that the arts institution could “end up being ripped down” if it didn’t have his support. The Trump administration has been a legal battle to allow the center to be renamed the “Trump-Kennedy Center” after his name be added to the building’s exterior, per board orders. A judge ordered his name be removed.

	“Yet the fight continued,” Streisand wrote. “After his name was removed, a humiliated Trump ordered a large tarp placed over the façade, where it remains today. The Trump-aligned board then relentlessly lobbied again to add his name, prompting another federal ruling that blocked their effort.

	“And now, a thoroughly defeated Trump has announced that the Kennedy Center is being closed for what the completely stacked board describes as a major renovation,” she continued. “Oddly, when Trump’s name was still on the building, there was no discussion of closing it!”
	

	Along with the statement, Streisand posted a black and white photo of her with Kennedy and another of her and Morgan Freeman at the Kennedy Center Honors ceremony.

	Streisand taped her “Funny Girl to Funny Lady” TV special at the Kennedy Center in 1975.

	Read Streisand’s full statement below.

	“In 1964, in the aftermath of President John F. Kennedy’s shocking assassination, Congress passed legislation designating the National Cultural Center as a living memorial to him.

	The Kennedy family and other American leaders wanted a meaningful way to preserve his legacy. Re-naming the Cultural Center in JFK’s honor was a fitting choice, because he was a true champion of the arts.

	Since then, the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts has stood as one of America’s great cultural venues. Many of the world’s most accomplished actors, musicians, singers and dancers have graced its stages.

	In 2008, I was deeply honored to be included in the 31st annual class of Kennedy Center Honorees. For me, and for so many artists, that honor represented something larger than a career recognition. It represented a belief in the importance of art to the life of a democracy.

	That is why what is happening to the Kennedy Center is so galling and painful to witness.

	When Donald Trump attempted to put his name alongside the late President Kennedy’s on the building’s entrance, the move was met with widespread opposition from artists and much of the public.

	A federal judge subsequently ruled that the Kennedy Center’s name could not be changed without an act of Congress, and Trump’s name was removed from the building’s façade.

	Yet the fight continued. After his name was removed, a humiliated Trump ordered a large tarp placed over the façade, where it remains today. The Trump-aligned board then relentlessly lobbied again to add his name, prompting another federal ruling that blocked their effort.

	And now, a thoroughly defeated Trump has announced that the Kennedy Center is being closed for what the completely stacked board describes as a major renovation. Oddly, when Trump’s name was still on the building, there was no discussion of closing it!

	You can easily imagine my indignation at seeing this revered institution become the subject of such a bitter struggle over one man’s name and unchecked ego.
	

	It is difficult not to think about what President Kennedy himself would have envisioned for the Center: not a monument frozen in time, but a living place where artists could challenge, inspire, provoke, and bring Americans together through the transformative power of the arts.

	The Kennedy Center was meant to pay tribute to a beloved president, and to advance his philosophy that artistic achievement was proof of a free society. He believed that when the creative impulse cannot flourish freely, a society loses its vitality.

	Yet another reason why it is so important that Americans exercise their right to vote in the upcoming midterm elections!”

schema.headline: Barbra Streisand Condemns Trump’s ‘Unchecked Ego’ Over Kennedy Center Name Battle: ‘Galling and Painful to Witness’

title: ‘The Simpsons’ Casting Director Scott Muller to Recruit Voices for Animated Film ‘The Most Serious Fart’
description: “The Simpsons” casting director Scott Muller will oversee voice casting for “The Most Serious Fart,” Utopai‘s animated feature based on Mike Bender’
body:
“The Simpsons” casting director Scott Muller will oversee voice casting for “The Most Serious Fart,” Utopai‘s animated feature based on Mike Bender’s bestselling children’s book, which wafts into theaters in 2027.

	“The Most Serious Fart” follows Siegfried, an uptight fart who is ashamed of who he is and determined to change farts into something respectable. Siegfried sets out on a journey that ultimately teaches him to accept himself, find friendship and discover fun along the way.
	

	“Voice casting will define how audiences first connect with Siegfried and the world around him,” Muller said in a statement. “Mike has created characters that invite bold comedy but also have a genuine emotional point of view. I am excited to find the voices that can make the humor land while giving the story the warmth and humanity at its center.”


	Muller has also worked as the casting director on “Futurama,” “King of the Hill” and the animated “Napoleon Dynamite” series. He is joined by “Coyote vs. Acme” story artist Andy Brooks as key story artist, Bender as writer, director and producer. Russell Hollander will also produce.

	Human animators and illustrators will lead the creative process and originate the film’s artwork. AI will be used selectively as a production tool to support iteration under their direction, Utopai said in a statement.

	“From the beginning, our goal has been to make a film that feels as distinctive as the book,” Bender said. “Scott understands how much performance shapes an animated world. Andy brings a remarkable ability to tell stories through character, expression and movement. Together with the rest of our creative team, they will help make Siegfried’s world feel completely original while keeping its heart intact.”

schema.headline: ‘The Simpsons’ Casting Director Scott Muller to Recruit Voices for Animated Film ‘The Most Serious Fart’

title: Empowering Content Libraries with AI is the New Future for Communal Fan Experiences, Execs Reveal: ‘You Have Companies Sitting on Crown Jewels’
description: Artificial intelligence has already made its mark on the screen. For some of the entertainment industry’s players, AI’s next playground is the real
body:
Artificial intelligence has already made its mark on the screen. For some of the entertainment industry’s players, AI’s next playground is the real world.

	Such was the focus on Thursday morning at the panel “Beyond the Screen: How AI is the Catalyst for Next-Gen Experiences” during Variety’s Entertainment & Technology Summit presented by EY. The session’s panelists – EY Americas’ Vamsi Duvvuri, the AI leader of its Technology, Media and Entertainment and Telecommunications division; Simon Robinson, Warner Bros. Discovery’s president of Global Experiences and Studio Operations; and Shari Reich, Nvidia’s Global Head of Audio and Music Developer Relations — broke down how AI doesn’t need to remain an exclusively individual experience, but instead one that spurs communal engagements and shared experiences.
	

	That starts with tapping into content libraries. Reich, whose work in the music industry includes stints at Sony Music and Warner Music Group, said companies can tap into their existing catalogues to help digitize and expand the use cases for things such as demos, video snippets and millions of tracks that she said they “don’t even know that literally are sitting in a warehouse.”


	“You have companies sitting on crown jewels,” Reich said. “To unlock all the things that you actually own, I think is going to be the next thing to gain fan experiences. To gain new discovery — I mean, a world full of things — but the thing is, that value is just really sitting right in your backyard.”

	Warner Bros. Discovery is trying to infuse some of that into its active live experiences, Robinson noted. At the company’s studio tour of its Burbank, California, lot, guests can interact with Superman’s robot aid “Gary,” a lovable presence from James Gunn’s 2025 blockbuster. Robinson said the experience in Superman’s Fortress of Solitude is currently programmed for about 15 minutes of engagement, after which the potential for repetition emerges. Moving forward, AI can help personalize how guests interact with either Gary or the Sorting Hat from the “Harry Potter” franchise, he said.
	

	“With the use of AI, we could completely structure that to make it a highly personalized and individual experience on a guest-by-guest basis,” he said.

	But the goal for the future should be bringing fans together beyond individualized experiences, the panelists said. “I always go back to the Eras Tour,” Robinson added. “10 million people didn’t buy a ticket to see Taylor Swift to have their own experience. They did it to be in a stadium with 10,000, 12,000 other people enjoying that moment. And I think that’s true throughout all of our worlds.”

	In music, Reich walked through her experience with Spotify’s AI-powered DJ tool, which precedes the streaming service’s upcoming AI remix tool. While much of the conversation surrounding AI and music centers on music generation, she said, personalized tools where fans can engage with songs and then share them represent another track in an AI-powered world.

	“It lives on the platform where you’re able to, [person-to-person], share remixing, and I think that that’s really cool and a really good example of personalization while also maintaining artist integrity,” she said. “You’re not going to tell them about some terrible remix somebody makes, but it’s still cool.”

	Still, Duvvuri warned that those experiences have to be thoughtful, not simply using AI for AI’s sake. People should be open to how AItools  can disrupt industries, but the choice to use them should be fueled by data and intentionality. 

	“There’s so much catalog there, but the effort to tag all the catalog and to figure out where the details are is still heavily manual,” he said. “AI can play a big role there if done properly, and it goes back to this idea of good AI requires good data. How do we collect the right data?”

	The panel was moderated by Jay Tucker, the executive director for the Center for Media, Entertainment and Sports at UCLA’s Anderson School. The daylong summit is being held at the Four Seasons in Beverly Hills.

schema.headline: Empowering Content Libraries with AI is the New Future for Communal Fan Experiences, Execs Reveal: ‘You Have Companies Sitting on Crown Jewels’

title: Fan Bingbing, Pedro Pascal, John Malkovich, Javier Bardem Films Lead Tokyo Festival’s Gala Selection
description: The Tokyo International Film Festival has named its 15-title Gala selection, headlined by Fan Bingbing in Wayne Wang’s “Diary of a Mad Old Man,” Ped
body:
The Tokyo International Film Festival has named its 15-title Gala selection, headlined by Fan Bingbing in Wayne Wang’s “Diary of a Mad Old Man,” Pedro Pascal in Tony Gilroy’s “Behemoth!,” John Malkovich in Martin McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine” and Javier Bardem in Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s “The Beloved.” 

	Wang’s film adapts Tanizaki Junichiro’s novel of the same name, relocating the story to present-day Tokyo, with Fan starring opposite Lily Franky and Kudoh Youki. Gilroy’s “Behemoth!” casts Pascal as a cellist alongside Olivia Wilde and Eva Victor.
	

	McDonagh’s “Wild Horse Nine,” also starring Sam Rockwell and Steve Buscemi, follows two CIA agents sent to Easter Island; Malkovich won the Venice Film Festival’s best actor award for the role. Bardem stars opposite Victoria Luengo in “The Beloved,” about an estranged father and daughter confronting old wounds during a new film project.


	Cristian Mungiu’s “Fjord,” winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve as members of a family relocating from Romania to Norway. Sode Yukiko’s “All the Lovers in the Night,” adapted from Kawakami Mieko’s novel, played in Un Certain Regard at Cannes ahead of its Tokyo bow.

	The festival’s opening film is “Sukiyaki,” with “Godzilla Minus Zero” screening as the centerpiece selection and “Colony” as the closing film.

	TIFF also unveiled a 12-title Animation Section, which includes three Japanese titles selected under the theme “Women Directors: Diverse Visions”: Nagaoka Chika’s “Detective Conan: The Fist of Blue Sapphire,” Watanabe Kotono’s “Gold Kingdom and Water Kingdom” and Yoshimura Ai’s “The Rose of Versailles.”
	

	The 39th Tokyo International Film Festival runs Oct. 26-Nov. 4, hosted by Unijapan. Market TIFFCOM runs alongside it from Oct. 28-30.

	FULL GALA SELECTION

	“All the Lovers in the Night” (Japan) – Directed by Sode Yukiko. Starring Kishii Yukino, Asano Tadanobu, Morita Misato.

	“Arrested Memory” (Taiwan/Japan) – Directed by SABU. Starring Ethan Juan, Hsieh Ying Xuan, Tsutsumi Shinichi.

	“Behemoth!” (U.S.) – Directed by Tony Gilroy. Starring Pedro Pascal, Olivia Wilde, Eva Victor.

	“The Beloved” (Spain) – Directed by Rodrigo Sorogoyen. Starring Javier Bardem, Victoria Luengo, Marina Foïs.

	“Bye Bye Love: Detective Is in the Bar” (Japan) – Directed by Shiraishi Kazuya. Starring Oizumi Yo, Matsuda Ryuhei, Suzuki Kyoka.

	“Diary of a Mad Old Man” (U.S.) – Directed by Wayne Wang. Starring Lily Franky, Fan Bingbing, Kudoh Youki.

	Displacement Film Fund screenings (U.K./Syria/Ukraine/Turkey/Iran/Germany/Somalia/Austria) – Directed by Hasan Kattan, Maryna Er Gorbach, Mohammad Rasoulof, Shahrbanoo Sadat and Mo Harawe.

	“Fjord” (Romania/France/Norway/Sweden/Denmark/Finland) – Directed by Cristian Mungiu. Starring Sebastian Stan, Renate Reinsve.

	“Sunshine Women’s Choir” (Taiwan) – Directed by Gavin Lin. Starring Ivy Chen, Judy Ongg, Sun Shumei.

	“Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” (U.S./Canada) – Directed by Jane Schoenbrun. Starring Hannah Einbinder, Gillian Anderson.

	“The Tiger and Her Wings the Movie” (Japan) – Directed by Nagikawa Yoshiro. Starring Ito Sairi, Okada Masaki, Matsumoto Koshiro.

	“Wild Horse Nine” (U.K./U.S./Chile) – Directed by Martin McDonagh. Starring John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, Steve Buscemi.

	“Your Story – Kimi No Hanashi” (Japan) – Directed by Nakagawa Ryutaro. Starring Kitamura Takumi, Deguchi Natsuki.

	“Cherry and Virgin” (Japan) – Directed by Kawajiri Masanao. Starring Okado Takashi, Kiyose Yaeko.

	“Iron Boy” (France) – Directed by Louis Clichy. Starring Gary Clichy, Rod Paradot, Dimitri Colas.

	“Son of a Bitch” (Brazil) – Directed by Érica Maradona, Otto Guerra, Tania Anaya and Sávio Leite. Starring Gabriel Martins, Matheus Nachtergaele, Zora Santos.

	“Walking with Animators” (France) – Directed by Alexandre Poncet and Gilles Penso. Starring Lucie Arnissolle, Will Becher, Doug Chiang.

title: A Generation Raised by ‘Judge Judy’: Judith Sheindlin Reflects on Her Long Run in TV, Shifting to Producing and Revving a ‘Baby Judy’ Series
description: If Judge Judith Sheindlin had never been profiled in a “60 Minutes” segment that caught the eye of a TV producer, and if she’d never made the segue
body:
If Judge Judith Sheindlin had never been profiled in a “60 Minutes” segment that caught the eye of a TV producer, and if she’d never made the segue into TV jurisprudence with “Judge Judy,” Sheindlin has no doubt what she would have done in the second half of her professional life.

	“I was comfortable. I loved the family court. I really did,” Sheindlin tells Variety. “It was a tough place to work, and I loved the work that I did there. It was important. Some you really did get an opportunity — if you broke sweat — and you were able to change a life. And that doesn’t happen to people often.”
	

	Sheindlin spoke to Variety in a wide-ranging interview about her 30-plus years in television in advance of the “Judge Judy: Unfiltered, Unforgettable,” a two-hour special celebrating her career that premieres Sept. 22 on CBS and Paramount+.



	Sheindlin’s signature style of dispensing no-nonsense rulings and life advice from the New York bench drew the attention of “60 Minutes” correspondent Morley Safer, who profiled her in a 1993 segment. That segment caught the attention of TV producer Larry Lyttle, who persuaded Sheindlin to try TV through his Big Ticket Television imprint, which was owned by Spelling Entertainment. (Paramount Pictures acquired Spelling in 1999.)

	“I would have stayed in the family court and that meant retirement at the age of 72,” Sheindlin reflects. “Maybe I would have worked as a judicial hearing office a couple of days a week. We would have moved down south where it was warm in the winter time – a beach condo. I think I would have been very happy, and fulfilled.”
	

	But that was not the destiny of the woman known to tens of millions of fans as Judge Judy. Her syndicated daytime court show single-handedly revived the court show genre after its premiere in 1996. She went on to become one of the most beloved and most-watched personalities in TV. At her peak, Sheindlin was among the highest-paid stars in all of television, commanding more than $45 million a year thanks to the boffo ratings for “Judge Judy.”

	After more than 30 years in television, Sheindlin has handed the on-air gavel to her son, Adam Levy, who launched his own daytime court show, “Adam’s Law,” with CBS on Sept. 14. Behind the scenes, however, Sheindlin is busier than ever as a producer with a half-dozen shows airing including “Adam’s Law,” the long-running “Hot Bench,” vintage episodes of “Judge Judy” and the “Judy Justice,” “Tribunal Justice” and “Justice on Trial” series that are available via Amazon Prime Video.

	Sheindlin’s latest endeavor is to develop content based on the enduring memes that feature a baby’s head superimposed on Sheindlin’s distinctive black robe with lace collar delivering plain-spoken advice. Those memes have zipped around the internet world since memes have existed. Sheindlin is hoping to tap into all of that existing energy for an animated series dubbed “Baby Judy.” She’s actively developing the property through her Queen Bee Productions banner.

	Sheindlin promises that the “Baby Judy” show she envisions will offer edgy takes that will get noticed.

	“The sizzle reel has to do with a young man looking for his first job, and he can’t get a job, even though he’s a college graduate,” she says. “He tells his prospective boss that he needs his own bathroom because he can’t share a bathroom because he has a smallish penis. The boss finally says to forget it, this is not the place for you. And so the job seeker sues him under the American for Disabilities Act, and then the case comes to me. That’s the setup.”

	The launch of “Adam’s Law” is a proud moment for Sheindlin, as a legal eagle and as a mother. Levy, a former district attorney for Putnam County in New York and a former defense attorney, had been a regular on “Tribunal Justice” for numerous seasons. That gave him the TV chops to take on his own Monday-Friday show. Sheindlin notes that mother and son take a very different approach to handling cases.
	

	“He likes to know everything about a case before he goes in. He likes to exhaust all the evidence and do whatever background information he can do on the litigants, so that he is fully informed, which means he spends hours and hours in preparation. That’s the way he has always walked as a litigator,” Sheindlin says. “I was a seat of the pants girl. I wasn’t an actress. If I were given a piece of evidence that I had was supposed to be seen for the first time, and would have to feign, ‘Oh my goodness, look at this.’ I couldn’t do it.”

	Beyond being a proud mom, Sheindlin has faith that Levy’s variation on the family business will be a success. She believes that the audience is still yearning for straightforward information about the law, and on a bigger plane, life guidance.

	“He believes in the law and he believes in the justice system, the concepts of law and order, right and wrong. And he’s smart as a whip,” she says. “Maybe 20 years from now, people are going to say, ‘Do you watch “Adam’s Law”?’ His mother had a show once.”

	Sheindlin believes wholeheartedly that authority figures can make a huge difference in an individual’s life. She still remembers the kindness she was shown by her sixth grade teacher as a kid growing up in New York.

	“Irving Bernstein made a difference in my life because one day after I was out of school for a day or two, he called the house to make sure I was OK,” Sheindlin recalls. “And that made me feel that he must think I’m special. I grew up with that sense that my sixth-grade teacher cared about me.”

	Undoubtedly, Sheindlin’s many bon mots and harsh-but-true zingers delivered from the bench have landed in a similar way for viewers.

	“I’m a responsibility girl. If you want to eat, you have to work. We like to think we come from a type of humanity that if you can’t walk and you need help, we help you and we keep you going. But if you can walk but choose not to walk, then I don’t want to have to support you.”

	The platform that Sheindlin has enjoyed on TV for a generation has been a powerful gift. These are among the themes explored in “Judge Judy: Unfiltered and Unforgettable,” which looks back at her long run on the TV bench but also looks ahead to what’s next for the indefatigable star.
	

	“I certainly have been handed the gift of having a second and third career that has not only been satisfying and gratifying, but it allowed me to deliver a message of the importance of good citizenry and taking care of yourself and personal responsibility,” she says. “You do that to make sure the next generation will be ever better off than you are. Those are the messages that I’ve been more than happy to deliver. And I’m still standing.”

title: Lady Gaga and Michael Polansky's Baby Is a Girl, Name Revealed
description:
Lady Gaga & Michael Polansky
                          We Have a Baby Girl!!!
body:
Lady Gaga & Michael Polansky
                          We Have a Baby Girl!!!
                          ... Name Revealed
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 17, 2026
                            11:23 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 17, 2026
                                12:23 PM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Lady Gaga and Michael Polansky's baby is a girl named Rose ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            According to the birth certificate obtained by TMZ, Rose Bean Polansky was born June 9 at 11:19 PM at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            It's unclear where the name Rose Bean originated from ... however Gaga has a large rose down her spine that she got to commemorate her performance of "La Vie En Rose" in the film "A Star is Born." The middle name Bean may have been inspired by singer/activist Carl Bean -- whom her hit "I Was Born This Way" pulled inspo from.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The baby was delivered by Dr. Robert Katz, the OB-GYN to the stars ... the same doctor who helped Ciara and Russell Wilson welcome their daughter, Sienna.
      
    
            As we reported ... Gaga was recently photographed holding her daughter close to her chest while walking with Polansky and a friend in Northern California. The couple has been spending private family time away from the spotlight.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Gaga and Polansky remain engaged and are not married ... despite a recent report claiming they had secretly tied the knot. Sources with direct knowledge told us earlier this month that close family members had seen the couple together and knew they had not gotten married.
      
    
            Gaga and Polansky got engaged in 2024. In March, Gaga said they planned to get married "soon."

title: Mike Sweetney, Ex-Georgetown Star, NBA Player, Dead At 43
description:
Mike Sweetney
                          Ex-Georgetown Star Dead At 43
                          F
body:
Mike Sweetney
                          Ex-Georgetown Star Dead At 43
                          Former Knicks Lottery Pick
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 17, 2026
                            12:17 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Mike Sweetney, the Georgetown big who was an NY Knicks lottery pick in 2003, has died.
      
    
            He was 43 years old.
      
    
            Sweetney's wife, India, announced the tragic news on social media on Thursday, writing her family was “deeply saddened” over the loss of her best friend of 30 years and hubby of 20.
      
    
            “His children were the light of his life,” India said.
      

                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            A cause of death hasn't been announced.
      
    
            Sweetney, who was born in Washington, D.C. and grew up in Maryland, tore up college basketball as a star at Georgetown, averaging 18.2 points and 9.2 rebounds per game.
      
    
            He was named First Team All-Big East as a Sophomore and Junior, before bolting for the draft.
      
    
            Sweetney was drafted 9th overall by the Knicks, but only spent two seasons in the Big Apple before spending two years in Chicago with the Bulls.
      
    
            Mike played four seasons in the Association, averaging 6.5 points and 4.5 rebounds, before hooping overseas for several years.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Sweetney retired in 2017.
      
    
            RIP

Elon Musk Documentary
                          Universal, We Have A Problem

                              September 17, 2026
                            11:37 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Universal's much-anticipated Elon Musk documentary may not have liftoff after all ... and it sounds like it could be grounded for good.
      
    
            There's no release date for "Musk" and there's a belief in Hollywood that Universal will ultimately decide against releasing the film altogether... according to The Hollywood Reporter.
      
    
            The documentary was shown at the Venice Film Festival earlier this month ... generating tons of headlines ... but the wider audience may be shut out.
      

            Elon's first wife, Justine Wilson, opened up in the documentary about their marriage, claiming her ex treated her as if she was just his employee.
      
    
            Justine says in the film ... "I learned the term 'gaslighting' through my relationship with Elon."
      
    
            Meanwhile, another one of Elon's exes, Ashley St. Clair, claimed she turned down a $40 million NDA so she could speak freely about him and appear in the film.
      
    
            However, the SpaceX founder told TMZ Ashley was never offered $40 million and "has a history of making false claims."
      
    
            We reached out to Universal ... so far no word back.
